title: KV cache compression roadtest and fidelity regression notebook
creator: Asha Patel
description: Field-style roadtest to evaluate compressed KV cache encodings (FP8 / INT8 / INT4) under continuous batching and realistic production traffic patterns. Goals: quantify GPU memory savings, measure downstream quality regressions on our eval prompt set, observe interactions between batching windows and KV decode overhead, and validate safe fallback thresholds for rolling canaries.
acceptance_criteria: End-to-end artifact: reproducible notebook + CI job that runs compression matrix on 3 model checkpoints
Clear memory savings numbers (median and P99 resident GPU memory) for FP8/INT8/INT4 across common sequence length buckets
Quality regression metrics reported (token logprob delta, normalized QA accuracy, and human preference sample) with statistical confidence
Performance SLOs: P95 generation latency within +10% of baseline for canary config, and P99 tail < 1.4x baseline
Automated fallback rule drafted (and unit-tested) that flips to FP16 cache when quality delta or logprob drop exceeds threshold on canary traffic
test_matrix: Compression modes: FP16 baseline, FP8 dynamic range, INT8 symmetric, INT4 packed
Batching configs: immediate (no batching), continuous batching window 10ms, 30ms, 50ms
Batch sizes observed: median request batch sizes from prod traces (1, 4, 8, 16)
Sequence length buckets: short <64, medium 64-512, long 512-2048
Workloads: synth-regression (2k prompts), prod-like chat-sim (10k sessions, interactive step length distribution), and cold-start long-context replay (500 traces)

Metrics: GPU resident memory (MiB), per-token decode CPU/GPU time, end-to-end latency p50/p95/p99, token-level avg logprob delta vs FP16, normalized QA accuracy on KV-regression-1000, human A/B sample size 200 for preference checks
results_summary: FP8: ~48% median GPU memory reduction versus FP16 on curated-13B-v2; p99 memory reduced by ~44%. Median latency +3ms at continuous batching 30ms; token logprob delta median -0.6% and QA accuracy delta -0.8% (statistically small but visible). Human A/B 200 samples: preference split 54/46 baseline vs fp8 (not significant at p<0.05).

INT8: ~62% median GPU memory reduction; p99 reduction ~58%. End-to-end median latency +8ms, p99 latency +15ms under 50ms batching window due to added unpacking overhead. Token logprob delta median -1.7%; QA accuracy drop ~-1.6%. Human A/B 200: baseline preferred 60/40 (marginal).

INT4: ~78% median GPU memory reduction; p99 reductions up to 72%. Noticeable quality impact: token logprob delta median -5.1%, QA accuracy -5.2%. High variance on long contexts where compaction noise compounds; human eval strongly prefers baseline in 82/18 split.

Batching interactions: small batching windows (10ms) amortize decode overhead poorly, increasing p99 latency for INT8/INT4; 30ms window gives best memory vs latency tradeoff. Larger batch sizes (>=8) improved throughput but slightly amplified INT4 degradation on long-context workloads due to accumulated quant error in KV lookups.

Failure modes: compressed KV misalignment observed when we applied block-packing across shards with different alignment rules (edge-case triggers at context boundaries); unpacking CPU spikes on nodes without optimized vectorized kernels increased jitter.
decisions: Adopt FP8 as the default compressed KV option for curated-13B-v2 canaries — acceptable memory reduction with minor quality delta
Hold off on automated INT4 rollouts for production; reserve INT4 for offline batch/offline inference where throughput and memory are prioritized over tight quality constraints
Introduce a required canary phase: 5% of traffic for 48 hours with per-route logprob monitoring and automatic rollback if token-level logprob drop > 1.5% and QA accuracy drop > 1.0%
Prioritize adding vectorized unpack kernels for INT8/INT4 on our serving nodes (ticket created) to reduce CPU unpack jitter
next_steps: Merge notebook -> ci job (PR: github.com/redwood-inference/infra/pull/2148) and schedule nightly runs against stale checkpoints
Create canary rollout flow: console feature flag + metrics augmentation (PRD: confluence.redwood.ai/kv-compression-canary)
Ticket to implement block-alignment guardrails in cache sharding logic (ENG-258900) — prevents misalignment failures across KV shards
Benchmark vectorized unpack kernels on our smallest CPU instance type and budget time for engineering spike (estimate 3d)
Run 5% canary for curated-13B-v2 FP8 on non-critical tenant group next week and collect A/B human eval samples
risks_and_mitigations: Risk: Silent quality regressions that are not captured by token-logprob. Mitigation: add route-level human review samples and a small automated QA harness covering hallucination-sensitive prompts.
Risk: Unpack CPU spikes causing latency SLO breaches. Mitigation: schedule kernel optimization and add backpressure to continuous batching if CPU queued > 70%
Risk: Shard misalignment corruption. Mitigation: add checksum and alignment detection at write/read time with automatic fallback to FP16 cache for mismatched shards
